# StreamBus ground truths (v2 user-centric API)

- Registration: `services.AddStreamBus((context, cfg) => ...)` for the
  default bus, `services.AddStreamBus<TBus>((context, cfg) => ...)` per
  extra bus. `IConfigurationSection` overload binds primitives; the code
  lambda adds types, routes, endpoints, retry.
- `cfg.Host(host, vhost, h => h.Credentials(user, password))` exactly
  once per bus. `guest` is always rejected. Defaults: StreamPort 5552,
  AmqpPort 5672 (queue dead letters only, else no AMQP connection),
  Heartbeat 60s always mapped, pools 1/1.
- Typed publish: `cfg.Publish<T>(stream)` for plain streams,
  `cfg.PublishSuper<T>(stream)` for super streams.
  `bus.PublishAsync(msg)` / `bus.PublishAsync(stream, msg)` are plain;
  `bus.PublishSuperAsync(msg, key)` /
  `bus.PublishSuperAsync(stream, msg, key)` are super with a required
  routing key. Wrong method for the registration is a config error.
  Same message type on two streams of one bus is an ambiguity error.
  Explicit-stream targets on undeclared streams raise
  `StreamBusStreamNotFoundException` and never auto-create.
  Raw bytes go through `bus.PublishRawAsync`.
- Consumer identity: `cfg.ReceiveEndpoint(stream, e =>
  e.Consumer<TConsumer>("group"))`. The group is required, verbatim,
  max 255 bytes, exactly one `Consumer` call per endpoint. Same group
  scales out via a shared cursor; different groups are independent
  cursors. Raw `ConsumeAsync` also requires `Reference`. The library
  never derives group names.
- Startup topology derives from explicit declarations plus endpoint and
  publish registrations. Endpoints without an explicit declaration adopt
  broker reality (matching kind consumed read-only, mismatch conflicts,
  missing declarable streams are declared, otherwise config error).
  Publish/endpoint kinds must agree with declarations.
- Retry: `cfg.UseMessageRetry(...)` global default, per-endpoint
  override, `UseRetry` escape hatches. Schedules: Immediate, Interval,
  Intervals, Exponential, None. Unbounded default retries forever.
- Exhaustion: bounded + `DeadLetterTo(name, type)` hands off; bounded +
  `OnExhausted` callback owns the outcome (return advances, throw
  recycles; declared destinations shadowed with a warning); bounded +
  neither hands off to the derived classic queue `{stream}_error`;
  unbounded + either is a config error.
- Error destinations: `DeadLetterType.Stream` (envelope + advance-once +
  `ReplayErrorStreamAsync`), `ClassicQueue` / `QuorumQueue` (durable,
  persistent, confirmed, `streambus.error.*` headers +
  `RequeueErrorsAsync`). Stream destinations must be explicitly
  declared; queue destinations are transport-declared.
- Startup blocking is service-level:
  `services.AddStreamBusHosting(h =>
  h.BlockStartupUntilReady(timeout?))`, at most once; default is
  non-blocking.
- Effectively-once (`ConsumeEffectivelyOnceAsync`) is unchanged.
- Startup topology derives from explicit declarations plus endpoint and
  publish registrations; endpoints without an explicit declaration adopt
  broker reality (match consumed read-only, mismatch conflicts, missing
  declarable declared, else config error). Single-partition reads are
  plain consumes of `{super}-{N}` with no declaration.
- Observability: `streambus` health check keyed `{vhost}|{busType}`;
  meter `StreamBus` (`streambus_partition_lag/_inflight/_retry_blocked`,
  `streambus_connection_state`, `streambus_offset_store_rejected_total`,
  `streambus_offset_regressed_total`, `streambus_offset_fallback_total`).
